### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**1** anchor(s) derived from **4** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them. ⚠️ **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/cli/src/utils/organization-ownership-grants.ts`, `packages/cli/src/utils/organization-ownership-plan.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/grant-set-name.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/cli/src/utils/organization-ownership-grants.ts`, `packages/cli/src/utils/organization-ownership-plan.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/grant-set-name.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **154** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json dd29bbe60df87727664424521c3a0b9eed37e985` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `c8260f80f9cbfa722821af20316009fe4263ec37` — the merge of head `9f50f1887b0f47ed778b3bff7f261d23831569a2` into base `dd29bbe60df87727664424521c3a0b9eed37e985`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin c8260f80f9cbfa722821af20316009fe4263ec37 && git checkout c8260f80f9cbfa722821af20316009fe4263ec37
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin dd29bbe60df87727664424521c3a0b9eed37e985 9f50f1887b0f47ed778b3bff7f261d23831569a2 && git checkout -B drift-repro dd29bbe60df87727664424521c3a0b9eed37e985 && git merge --no-ff 9f50f1887b0f47ed778b3bff7f261d23831569a2

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json dd29bbe60df87727664424521c3a0b9eed37e985
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `55725c1d79fc4f4cefd8b4d8af2bed06a63fadb9`
Local-runs: none

PR #23624 at the head the brief named (it has not moved): merge base `dd4ef38506`, 3 commits, 10 files, +45/-28. The REST file list and `git diff origin/main...head` agree. Read through refs only.

### ① Derived judgments

**Item 2: the remedy texts.**
- The CLI's flags on `origin/main` (`packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/organization-ownership.ts`, `static flags`) are `database-url`, `out`, `json`, `apply`, `plan-file`, `backup-taken`, `template-choice`, `metadata-choice` and `fate-supplement`. None has an alias. There is no `plan` flag: "`--plan`" appears only in the docblock, as the ADR's name for the bare read-only mode. `--out` is the plan mode's file flag (with `--apply` it names the report). The dev's disproof holds.
- `runApply` refuses a run without `--plan-file` (`plan-file-required`). Both texts now give the shape the CLI accepts: plan with `--out plan.json`, review the file, run `--apply --plan-file plan.json`, then restart. That holds for the `logReport` line in `catalog-reference-report.ts` and for the `replacement` of `ups-permission-set-id-column-retired`.
- **The spelling is identical to S4's entry only for the plan step.** S4's entry `cli-organization-ownership-apply-plan-file-required` writes the plan step as `os migrate organization-ownership --out plan.json` and says "review the file it writes". This PR uses the same words. The apply step differs:
  - S4's entry, S4's pending note `15211-cli-apply-reviewed-plan.md` and the CLI's `examples` all spell it `--apply --backup-taken --plan-file plan.json`.
  - This PR's three texts spell it `--apply --plan-file plan.json`.
  - The CLI still accepts the PR's spelling, but only at a terminal. Without `--backup-taken`, the CLI's local `confirm` asks the backup question and goes on after a yes. A run with no TTY, or with `--json`, is refused with `backup-unacknowledged`. That refusal comes before any write and names the flag.
  - The card's wanted text and the CLI's own `plan-file-required` remedy also leave the flag out.
  - The PR body's claim "the spelling of S4's own entry" covers only the plan step, and it is true for that step.
  - Non-blocking: see ③ flag 8.
- No plugin-security or spec test asserts either text, so no pin is owed. This matches the card.

**The pending-note correction.**
- `.changeset/23430-grant-permission-set-id-retired.md` sits in `.changeset/` on both `main` and the head. It is not among the 582 files in `.changeset/pre/`. No `CHANGELOG.md` carries its text: `runOneTimeGrantPermissionSetNameBackfill` appears in none. It is pending.
- The diff to that note has numstat 2/2: line 21 (FROM → TO) and line 27 ("What else changes"). Both now say `--out plan.json`, and line 21 says `--apply --plan-file plan.json`. Nothing else changed: the frontmatter (three `minor`), `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` and the `adr-0087` marker are untouched.
- `Check Changeset` failed three times on this head (PR Automation runs 38691420251, 38691572183 and 38691702287). Each failed at step 12, "Reject an empty-frontmatter changeset added by this PR", with one file annotation, and every annotation names only `.changeset/23430-grant-permission-set-id-retired.md` (the #17712 COLLISION vs DELIBERATE CORRECTION refusal).
  - Steps 11 (require a changeset), 13 (ADR-0087 disposition) and 15 (no major) pass.
  - It is not a COLLISION: the PR's own note has its own name, `23513-grant-remedy-plan-file.md`.
  - The PR has no `skip-changeset` label, as #18375 ruling D requires.
  - So the red names only the deliberate correction.

**Item 3: is each reworded comment true on main plus this PR?**
- **`grantKey` (`organization-ownership-grants.ts`) and `GrantKeyPlan` (`-plan.ts`): true.**
  - On `main`, the grant's index is `{ fields: ['user_id', 'permission_set', 'organization_id'], unique: 'organization' }` (`sys-user-permission-set.object.ts:267`).
  - ADR-0120 D3 builds that index's organization key part as `COALESCE(organization_id, '__global__')`, so a NULL organization is one key. `JSON.stringify([user, name, null])` keys it the same way.
  - Neither comment names the retired door any more.
- **The apply-test title (`:1981`): true.** The test inserts two NULL-organization grants of one set and asserts a column-drops blocker of 2 grants in 1 group. GROUP BY keys the NULLs together, as D3 says the index does. Only the title string changed, and "unlike the index" no longer appears anywhere on the head.
- **The plugin-auth `grant-set-name.ts` header: true.**
  - C7b S3 (#23503) retired the column.
  - The backfill has no definition or call left on the head. Two plugin-security test comments mention it only in the past tense.
  - "No boot names a grant" holds.
  - The rewrite does list each grant it does not name, with a reason: `GrantRewritePlan.reasons` is keyed by `UnnamedReason`, and `collisions` name both ids.
  - The header names `os migrate organization-ownership --apply` as the act that names a grant, not as a command to run. That is the PR's declared left-as-written class.
- **The `persistGrantNameBackfillRecord` removal: complete.**
  - `git grep` finds zero references anywhere on the head.
  - It left `DURABILITY_CRITICAL_CALLEES` and the census's `WRITE_SHAPED_CALLEES` gate-vocabulary copy together, so the copy-vs-declaration cross-check still matches.
  - Neither script nor any baseline hard-codes the count: both print `copiedGateNames.length`.
  - Since the merge base, `main` changed the gate only in a comment (9a6f790a38, #23612). It touches no map entry.

**No behaviour change: confirmed.** The only executable changes are:
- the `logReport` string literal (still `logError`, fields `{ count, organizations }`);
- the entry's `replacement` string (`id`, `surface`, `reason` and `acceptanceCriteria` unchanged);
- one test-title string;
- the two map entries for a callee that no longer exists.

Everything else is comments and changesets. Nothing under `skills/**` is touched.

### ② Semver level

`patch` for `@objectstack/plugin-security` (log text) and `@objectstack/spec` (one entry's prose value) is correct under WHICH LEVEL. The PR adds no export, key or accepted value, and "a `fix(` that changes no public surface stays `patch`". The PR body and the changeset both read `Clause-②: no`, so the level axis stands down. No `major`. `@objectstack/cli` and `@objectstack/plugin-auth` change only comments and a test title, and correctly release nothing.

### ③ Boundary flags

From 6185759753 and the patch round (55725c1d79):
1. **`--plan` disproved, `--out plan.json` used.** Confirmed from the flag definitions (①). Answered.
2. **The "consumed or published" premise was false: the note is pending.** Confirmed (①). The open question was answered A in the patch round, and the correction is limited to two sentences. Still owed: the DELIBERATE CORRECTION remedy needs the confirmation written on the PR. The body states it; the seat's ACCEPT must carry the confirmation (precedent Q-S4 → A, 6164948359).
3. **NOT MEASURED locally: the cli unit tier.** CI's Test Core: all six shards and the `Test Core` roll-up concluded `success` on this head. Measured by CI; closed.
4. **`check:dual-build-cjs-loads` and `check:i18n-coverage` answered exit 3 first (prerequisite only), then 0.** Not re-judged here. CI's Lint & Repo Gates is green on this head.
5. **Zero label writes, and no `skip-changeset`.** Correct under #18375 ruling D.
6. **The commit trailer.** All three commits carry the model-free `Co-authored-by: Claude` with `Claude-Session`. No commit carries a model id.
7. **Left as written.** Comments and docs that name `--apply` as the act: I read the two mdx lines (`permission-sets.mdx:397`, `capabilities.mdx:220`). They describe the act and give no instruction. Agreed; no carrier needed.

New from this review:

8. **The `--backup-taken` divergence (non-blocking; the seat rules).** The three texts spell the apply step without `--backup-taken`. The S4 entry and S4's note spell it with the flag, and both will appear in the same CHANGELOG. What happens:
   - At a terminal, the CLI accepts the PR's spelling after the backup question.
   - In a script (no TTY), the run is refused with `backup-unacknowledged`, nothing is written, and the refusal names the flag.

   Either accept this as the interactive form at ACCEPT, or add one word in each of the three places in a patch round.
9. **S2 #23469 is still open.** It overlaps this PR only in the `GrantKeyPlan` doc comment in `organization-ownership-plan.ts`. Whichever lands second merges `main`. This head merges cleanly with `main` today.
10. **The PR is still a draft.** The seat flips it before the queue.

CI on this head: 55 check-runs, read at 2026-10-15T06:49Z: 42 success, 10 skipped, 3 failure, none running. The only failures are the three `Check Changeset` runs, by design (①). `Test Core` (1/6 to 6/6 and the roll-up), all four `Type Check` lanes (source gates, debt ledger, consumer gates, workspace), `Build Core` and `Lint & Repo Gates` with its lanes are green.

**Seat adoption** (2026-10-15T07:05Z). Adopted after an audit of the reviewer transcript: one Write, to this record; 52 Bash calls, all reads (`git show`, `git diff`, an in-memory `git merge-tree`, REST GETs); one Monitor polling the check-runs; no MCP call, no GitHub write, no worktree, build or test run.

**The head moved after this record, and the seat verified the delta itself.** `git diff 55725c1d79 9f50f1887b` touches 4 files, +7 / −7. The only change is `--backup-taken` inserted into the apply step in five places:
- `catalog-reference-report.ts` `logReport`, whose string is re-wrapped with its text otherwise unchanged;
- the `ups-permission-set-id-column-retired` entry's `replacement`;
- #23503's pending note, line 21;
- this PR's own changeset (title and line 15).

This aligns the apply step with S4's entry, S4's note and the CLI's examples, so a non-TTY caller is not refused `backup-unacknowledged`. That answers this record's non-blocking `--backup-taken` point.

**The landing prechecks on `9f50f1887b`:**
- CI is green except `Check Changeset`. Its one annotation names only `.changeset/23430-grant-permission-set-id-retired.md`, under the DELIBERATE CORRECTION class.
- `check-governed-merges.mjs` reports no governed path.
- `git merge-tree` against `origin/main` exits 0.
- The only closing keyword is `Fixes #23513`.

**The seat confirms the DELIBERATE CORRECTION.** #23503's note is still pending (it is not in `.changeset/pre/`, and no CHANGELOG carries it). Its lines 21 and 27 named a bare `--apply`, which the CLI refuses, and a `--plan` flag, which does not exist. They now name the real ceremony: `--out plan.json`, review, then `--apply --backup-taken --plan-file plan.json`. The precedent is Q-S4 → A on #15211 (6164948359). `Check Changeset` is red by design for this alone: it is not a required queue context, and this comment records the gate and its reason.

Reviewed-by: `session_01ADzJtzYTLUfgrRZHxkagkX`

**VERDICT: PASS**
